events.text: They come to you before you have learned where to stand: four envoys of four pantheons, each carrying a light. One is gold and does not flicker. One is so dim you only see it when you look away. One is green and smells of rain. One crackles. None of them bows. They circle you as buyers circle a horse, and each says the same thing in a different voice: the gods have seats, and a newcomer may be let to earn one.

choices.text: Go with the envoy whose light is the colour of your Dao

effects.log: You follow the light that knows your Dao. It leads you to a hall where nobody makes room for you yet.

choices.text: Go with the envoy who knew your name above the clouds

effects.log: One envoy has heard of you from the Upper Realm, and says so as if it were a small thing. You go with that one.

choices.text: Thank them all, and choose later

effects.log: You thank the envoys and send them home. The pantheons will wait: the gods have nothing but time.

choices.text: Stand alone among the gods

effects.log: You bow to all four lights and follow none of them. A god without a pantheon is rare, and watched, and free.

events.text: The heralds of your pantheon go down every golden road at once, blowing horns that sound like thunder heard from inside a cloud. It is war in heaven: a star that both pantheons claim, and ten thousand years of grudges riding on it. Your pantheon looks at you to see what you will do.

choices.text: Take your place at the front

effects.log: You ride to the front before the horns have stopped, and your pantheon sees you go.

choices.text: Go to both pantheons and ask for peace

effects.log: You walk into the hall of the enemy alone and ask them to put the star down.

choices.text: Keep to your own domain and let the war pass

effects.log: You stay where you are. Wars in heaven are long, and you have learned to be longer.

events.text: One of the domains you took from a god stirs like a field before a storm. The god who held it has come back, older and angrier, and stands at its border asking for it by name. Behind the god, a pantheon is watching to see how the question is answered.

choices.text: Meet the god at the border and defend it

effects.log: You go out to the border of the domain alone.

choices.text: Give the domain back with both hands

effects.log: You open your hands, and the domain goes home to the one who held it first.

choices.text: Appeal to your pantheon to stand behind you

effects.log: You send word to your pantheon and wait at the border for its answer.

events.text: A god throws a feast that has been going on since before the world below had seasons. You are invited, which means you are expected to bring something. The other guests have brought a comet, a lost language and a very old wine.

choices.text: Bring a memory of the world below

effects.log: You bring the taste of a street dumpling from a life long ago. The gods have never had one. They ask for more.

choices.text: Bring a single perfect form of your art

effects.log: You stand up and show one form, slowly. The feast goes quiet for the length of it, and then louder than before.

choices.text: Bring nothing, and listen

effects.log: You bring nothing and listen all night. You learn more than anyone who brought a comet.

events.text: A god so young that the domain still hangs off them like a borrowed robe asks to walk with you for a while. They have a domain of small rains, and no idea what to do with it, and a great fear of getting it wrong.

choices.text: Teach them what the Dao taught you

effects.log: You walk with the young god for a year. By the end of it the small rains fall exactly where they are needed.

choices.text: Tell them that every god starts by getting it wrong

effects.log: You tell them about your own first mistakes. They laugh for the first time in a century, and rain falls, warm.

choices.text: Send them back to their pantheon

effects.log: You send the young god home kindly. It is not your domain to teach, and you know it.

events.text: A river runs between the stars here, slow and silver, and on its far bank there is nothing at all: not darkness, not light, only the edge of everything that has been made so far. A ferryman who is also a god offers to take you across and back.

choices.text: Cross, and look at the edge of making

effects.log: You stand on the far bank for a moment that lasts a year. When you come back, your Dao is quieter and deeper.

choices.text: Sit on this bank and watch the river

effects.log: You sit by the river of stars and let it go by. Some of its quiet stays with you.

choices.text: Ask the ferryman who made the river

effects.log: The ferryman says nobody made it: it is what is left over when a world is finished. You think of your own world.

events.text: Somewhere in a world you have never seen, someone has started praying to you by name. The prayer is small and clumsy and very sincere, and it arrives in the Divine Realm like a pebble in a still pool.

choices.text: Answer it, a little

effects.log: You send a little luck down the prayer like water down a string. Far away, a harvest does not fail.

choices.text: Listen to it, and keep it

effects.log: You do not answer. You keep the prayer, and take it out sometimes, and it never stops being sincere.

choices.text: Let it go to a god whose domain it is

effects.log: You pass the prayer to the god of that world's fields, who answers it better than you could.

events.text: From the height of the Divine Realm you can see the whole road you came up: the world below, the clouds, the jade stairs, the throne. Far down, at the end of the cloud road, a plain wooden gate stands half open, as it always did.

choices.text: Look at it a long while

effects.log: You look at the gate you never walked through until it is only a gate again. Then you go back to being a god.

choices.text: Send a light down the road for whoever climbs next

effects.log: You set a small light on the jade stairs. Some immortal, one day, will climb by it and not know why.

choices.text: Turn your back on the road

effects.log: There is nothing down there you need. You turn and walk further into the gold.
